genres.definition: 面向消费者公开传播的完整品牌商业广告成片，通常在较短时长内建立传播命题、呈现产品或品牌利益，并以品牌资产或行动指向收束。TVC 描述的是商业广告成片心智，不限定必须高端、电影感或以产品特写为主。
genres.include_when: 能明确回答广告在向谁传播什么品牌或产品主张，并具有广告化开场、推进和品牌收束。
genres.exclude_when: 品牌支持教程、售后排错、发布会实录、媒体测评、幕后花絮和纯企业介绍不能只因品牌官方发布就标为 TVC。

genres.chinese: 概念片 / 品牌宣言片
genres.definition: 围绕品牌精神、态度或核心命题，用视觉隐喻、象征、情绪和节奏传达抽象概念；产品可以弱露出，重点是让观众记住品牌立场而非具体功能。
genres.include_when: 品牌主张或抽象命题是叙事中心，画面主要承担情绪和观念表达。
genres.exclude_when: 只有高级画面但没有品牌命题的产品 B-Roll，以及以企业历史和员工采访为主的 Corporate Film。

genres.chinese: 企业宣传 / 品牌故事片
genres.definition: 通过创始人、员工、工艺、历史、组织能力或真实人物材料回答品牌是谁、为何存在以及如何创造价值，常结合采访、档案或纪录片式素材。
genres.include_when: 企业身份、使命、历史或组织能力是主要信息，而非某个产品的直接购买理由。
genres.exclude_when: 虚构剧情推销单一产品应归 Story-Driven Product Ad；核心模板库还需另行排除过长、采访主导和纪录片慢叙事样片。

genres.definition: 以产品和场景的质感镜头、光影、景深、运动和构图形成连续视觉段落，文字和讲解较少，主要价值是氛围与审美，而非完整故事或信息教学。
genres.include_when: 多个审美化补充镜头共同构成成片主体，即使单个镜头也可能同时包含产品细节。
genres.exclude_when: 只有一个普通产品近景；微距细节主导时归 Macro Close-Up；完整外观识别主导时归 Multi-Angle Showcase。

genres.definition: 通过极近距离画面放大材质、纹理、接缝、工艺、微小结构或细微运动，让肉眼不易察觉的产品细节成为主要视觉信息。
genres.include_when: 微距或超近景细节是连续且有表达价值的主要段落。
genres.exclude_when: 普通近景、单一静物、常规手持展示或仅把产品放大裁切，不能单独成立本标签。

genres.definition: 以产品为主要主体，通过正面、侧面、背面、顶部、底部、旋转、翻转或结构展开，帮助观众完整认识外观、比例、接口和设计。
genres.include_when: 至少从多个有信息差的角度连续呈现同一产品，观看目的主要是认识产品设计。
genres.exclude_when: 单一角度转场、普通手持晃动、微距细节或功能操作不能仅因镜头在移动就成立。

genres.definition: 在产品展示或使用画面中，用可见文字、参数、图标、箭头、局部放大、动态图形或结构示意明确指出卖点、功能和用户利益，并让信息层与画面同步。
genres.include_when: 观众静音观看时仍能从可见信息层识别至少一个具体卖点或利益点。
genres.exclude_when: 操作步骤编号、连接说明、设置菜单和排错指令属于 How-To 信息，不因出现文字就自动成为 Feature Callout；只有口头介绍也不成立。

genres.definition: 用左右、上下或多窗口在同一时间轴同步呈现两组相关画面，形成产品与场景、整体与细节、不同视角或两种结果之间的明确对照或互补。
genres.include_when: 分屏是持续可识别的主要表现机制，并且两侧内容存在有意义的关系。
genres.exclude_when: 普通顺序剪辑、一次性画中画或没有比较关系的装饰性拼贴不成立；有公平实测过程时还可标 Comparison Test。

genres.definition: 通过可见的执行动作、产品响应和结果，演示一个或多个功能如何工作，重点是让观众理解能力和效果，而不是教会完整操作流程。
genres.include_when: 至少存在一个完整的动作到响应或结果的因果链，产品功能被实际展示而非仅被描述。
genres.exclude_when: 只列参数、只展示外观不成立；需要观众按顺序跟做才能完成任务时，主题材应为 How-To Tutorial。

genres.definition: 把安装、连接、佩戴、设置、操作或维护任务拆成可按顺序执行的步骤，使观众能够跟随完成明确任务。
genres.include_when: 存在明确任务目标、顺序步骤、操作证据和完成状态，步骤之间不能随意调换。
genres.exclude_when: 快速展示多个功能但不要求跟做属于 Product Demo；品牌支持教程即使分类成立，也不自动具备品牌品宣或核心模板资格。

genres.definition: 沿包装开启顺序呈现外包装、拆封、开盖、取出产品、配件和初次上手，以包装结构、首次发现和期待感构成主要内容。
genres.include_when: 包装从关闭到打开的过程真实可见，取出产品和配件构成连续段落。
genres.exclude_when: 桌面陈列、包装静物、产品展示或标题写有 unboxing 但没有实际开启过程，均不成立。

genres.chinese: 试穿 / 试戴 / 试用
genres.definition: 展示产品上身、上脸、穿戴、佩戴或由用户实际试用后的外观、贴合、操控和即时体验，核心问题是产品用在我身上或手里是什么样。
genres.include_when: 穿戴或试用过程以及人体上的结果是主要段落，适用于美妆、服饰、配饰、可穿戴设备和可直接体验的产品。
genres.exclude_when: 仅出现人物持有产品、单纯生活场景或只演示功能而不呈现试用体验，不能成立。

genres.definition: 通过模特、造型、配色、场景和音乐展示一个系列或多种组合的整体风格，观看重点是造型搭配和审美选择，而不是单次试穿过程。
genres.include_when: 至少有多套造型、多个搭配或明确系列化风格展示，产品承担造型表达。
genres.exclude_when: 明星出镜、单一佩戴镜头、一次试穿或普通生活方式广告不自动构成 Lookbook。

genres.definition: 在紧凑的晨间、通勤、工作、运动、旅行或夜间等连续生活流程中，让产品在一个或多个自然节点被使用，表达产品如何融入日常。
genres.include_when: 能够识别连续流程和至少两个生活节点，产品使用与流程存在自然关系。
genres.exclude_when: 一个生活化镜头、单一使用场景或从人物生活背景娓娓道来的纪录片慢叙事不成立核心模板；后者即使有日常元素也不计本题材供给。

genres.definition: 先把目标用户的具体问题或不便可视化，再让产品介入，并呈现问题被解决后的结果，形成清晰的痛点到解决方案因果链。
genres.include_when: 问题、产品介入和解决结果三个环节均可被识别，产品对结果具有直接作用。
genres.exclude_when: 泛泛表达焦虑、只列卖点、没有解决结果或产品与问题没有因果关系时不成立。

genres.definition: 明确呈现同一对象使用产品前的问题状态、使用过程和使用后的结果，通过画面、数据、构图或状态差异让变化可直接比较。
genres.include_when: 同一对象或同一条件下的前后状态均有证据，变化能够被观众直接识别。
genres.exclude_when: 不同产品之间的公平测试应归 Comparison Test；只有分屏形式但没有前后状态证据不成立。

genres.definition: 让本产品与竞品、旧型号或传统方案在相同条件下完成同一测试，公开展示测试条件、过程、结果和结论，以可见证据证明差异。
genres.include_when: 比较对象、统一条件、测试过程和结果至少能够被画面或数据核验。
genres.exclude_when: 没有实际测试的口头比较、参数表、外观并列或装饰性分屏不成立。

genres.definition: 通过人物、场景、需求或冲突、转折和结局构成完整故事，产品作为关键道具、能力或解决方案参与故事因果。
genres.include_when: 观众能复述基本故事，且移除产品会破坏关键因果或结局。
genres.exclude_when: 企业历史和真实组织故事归 Corporate Film；只有氛围蒙太奇或产品展示而没有叙事因果不成立。

genres.definition: 以短剧观看体验为主，包含较完整的人物关系、对话、冲突、高潮和解决，可采用喜剧、温情、悬疑或讽刺调性，产品自然嵌入并推动剧情。
genres.include_when: 叙事体量明显高于普通短广告，人物关系和戏剧推进是主要观看动力。
genres.exclude_when: 只有一个简短情节或单次反转更适合 Story-Driven Product Ad 或 Conflict & Twist Ad；超过核心库时长门槛的完整版只进灵感库。

genres.definition: 先建立争执、误会、预期或社会情境冲突，再由产品触发意外但可理解的反转，以冲突和反转形成核心记忆点。
genres.include_when: 冲突铺垫、产品介入和反转三个环节均成立，反转依赖产品或品牌信息。
genres.exclude_when: 普通剧情结局、无铺垫笑点或与产品无关的反转不成立。

genres.definition: 围绕运动员或普通人的训练、比赛、转变与关键高光，用动作、现场氛围、音乐和品牌精神塑造力量感与英雄感。
genres.include_when: 人物的体育行动和高光时刻驱动主要情绪，并与品牌或产品主张建立关系。
genres.exclude_when: 普通产品运动场景、功能演示或从人物人生慢慢铺陈的长纪录片不能仅因有运动员而成立核心模板。

genres.definition: 用手机竖屏、手持、自然光、生活场景和口语表达模拟普通用户原生内容，同时有设计过的钩子、痛点、产品使用、证据和行动引导。
genres.include_when: 内容整体遵循平台原生用户内容语法，而不是只在正式广告中插入一个自拍视频。
genres.exclude_when: 精致品牌大片、无商业信息的普通用户视频或单纯正面口播不成立；来源类型仍需与题材标签分开记录。

genres.definition: 由真实或拟真的使用者以第一人称表达使用经历、优缺点、结果和推荐理由，并以具体产品体验建立信任。
genres.include_when: 个人使用证言和评价是主要说服机制，能够识别具体体验或结果。
genres.exclude_when: 只有品牌功能讲解、没有个人体验评价时更接近 Talking Head 或 Product Demo；独立媒体长测评不具备品牌品宣资格。

genres.definition: 通过朋友之间的自然对话和互动完成产品安利，通常包括需求被提起、朋友拿出产品、演示或共同体验以及对方反应。
genres.include_when: 朋友关系和互动是信任与推荐的主要来源，至少有两人发生有效产品对话。
genres.exclude_when: 单人面对镜头推荐归 Testimonial 或 UGC；没有产品安利关系的普通多人剧情不成立。

genres.definition: 人物在行走或场景移动中以自拍、跟随或第一人称视角自然讲述体验、痛点或推荐，并穿插持有和使用产品的动作。
genres.include_when: 移动中的连续口述是主要结构，环境变化和产品表达共同推进内容。
genres.exclude_when: 传统 TVC 中的人物走路镜头、静态口播或只有移动镜头但没有分享表达不成立；品牌官方不是该题材成立的必要条件。

genres.definition: 由采访者围绕产品或品牌相关问题向不同人物提问，并通过多个人物的回答、反应和观点切换形成内容。
genres.include_when: 采访关系和多人物观点是主要结构，问题在不同回答之间保持一致或相关。
genres.exclude_when: 单人系统讲解归 Talking Head；品牌纪录片中的零散采访若不形成独立访谈结构，不作为核心次标签。

genres.definition: 以一个或多个明确问题组织内容，由专家、用户或品牌代表回答消费者疑问、解释选择标准，并以产品、演示或结论完成回答。
genres.include_when: 问题以文字或口头方式明确出现，后续内容逐一作答，问题是结构而非装饰。
genres.exclude_when: 没有明确问题的访谈、口播、测评或功能介绍不成立。

genres.definition: 由一位人物正面对镜头承担主要信息输出，通常包含开场、分点说明、少量产品画面穿插和结论，人物的表达是内容主体。
genres.include_when: 大部分信息依靠单人正面讲话传递，移除口播后内容明显不完整。
genres.exclude_when: 多人采访、移动 Vlog 或舞台演讲应归其他题材；标签成立不代表适合当前 AI 核心模板库。

genres.chinese: 发布会短讲 / 专家演讲
genres.definition: 由演讲者在舞台、发布会或专业演示环境中，以观点、数据、案例、产品论证和结论介绍产品或知识，常配合大屏、图表或现场演示。
genres.include_when: 舞台化或正式演讲关系是主要观看心智，演讲者面向现场或专业语境进行结构化表达。
genres.exclude_when: 普通室内正面口播归 Talking Head；完整发布会、直播回放和长演讲只证明题材存在，不进入核心模板库。

genre_groups.name: 品牌表达类
genre_groups.description: 以品牌、商业传播成片或品牌主张为主要观看预期。

genre_groups.name: 产品视觉类
genre_groups.description: 以产品外观、材质、结构和画面信息层为主要内容。

genre_groups.name: 功能与体验类
genre_groups.description: 以功能如何工作、如何操作或首次接触体验为主要内容。

genre_groups.name: 场景与生活方式类
genre_groups.description: 以穿搭、审美组合或连续生活流程中的产品使用为主要内容。

genre_groups.name: 说服与证明类
genre_groups.description: 以痛点、效果变化或可见测试证据建立购买理由。

genre_groups.name: 剧情与人物品牌类
genre_groups.description: 以虚构故事、冲突反转、品牌真实故事或体育人物高光驱动观看。

genre_groups.name: 真人原生表达类
genre_groups.description: 以用户、朋友、采访者、专家或演讲者的真人表达关系为主要内容。

categories.definition: 以蜂窝通信和移动计算为核心的手持设备；折叠屏手机仍归本类，不把手机壳、充电配件或跨设备套装计入。

categories.definition: 以触控大屏为主要交互、可独立运行操作系统的平板设备；不含便携显示器和数位板。

categories.definition: 带实体键盘、可独立运行桌面操作系统的便携电脑；二合一设备以广告主卖点和主使用形态判断。
categories.search_route: Apple MacBook / Dell XPS / Lenovo / ASUS：发布片、设计片、功能演示

categories.definition: 具备应用、通知、健康或运动能力的腕上智能设备；强调完整智能系统和手表形态。
categories.search_route: Apple Watch / Galaxy Watch / Pixel Watch / Garmin：功能片、运动场景片

categories.definition: 用于寻找物品、宠物或行李位置的蓝牙/UWB/GPS 标签与追踪设备；不含运动手环。
categories.search_route: Apple AirTag / Samsung SmartTag / Tile：场景问题解决片

categories.definition: 佩戴在头部、提供虚拟现实或增强现实体验的独立或连接式头显；智能眼镜按主要体验归入。

categories.definition: 通过音频线或数据接口连接的入耳式、半入耳式耳机；头戴式产品不按连接方式归入本类。

categories.definition: 以头梁和耳罩为主要形态的耳机，不按有线或无线技术拆分；降噪、游戏与监听款均可归入。
categories.search_route: Sony WH / Bose QC / Beats / Marshall / Dyson：TVC、功能片、设计片

categories.definition: 面向个人或家庭播放的便携蓝牙音箱及紧凑型无线音箱；不含电视音响系统和专业扩声设备。
categories.search_route: JBL / Marshall / Sonos / Bose：场景片、产品片、功能演示

categories.definition: 用于录音、直播、会议或内容创作的独立麦克风及无线麦克风系统；不含耳机内置麦克风。

categories.definition: 以静态摄影为主要心智的数码相机、微单、卡片机和即时成像相机；不含手机和运动相机。
categories.search_route: Canon / Sony Alpha / Nikon / Fujifilm / Polaroid：产品片、摄影作品片

categories.definition: 强调防抖、防水、第一视角和户外运动记录的小型相机；全景运动相机归入本类。
categories.search_route: GoPro / DJI Osmo Action / Insta360：运动高光、功能演示

videos.description:
PNC Bank is tapping into an organic fan movement at PNC Park in Pittsburgh by serving up limited-edition ice cream (traffic) cones to Pittsburgh Pirates fans on select game days this season.

Created in partnership with AOR Arnold, the promotion pays tribute to the now famous “Hoist the Cone” rallying cry, which originated from a misprinted shirt reading “Hoist the Cone” instead of “Hoist the Colors.” Pirates fans embraced the unexpected slogan, and the orange traffic cone has become a recognizable symbol of Pittsburgh Pirates team spirit and local pride since.

With real traffic cones recently disappearing from city streets as fans hunted for gear to hoist at games, PNC stepped in to give the hometown crowd a safer, smarter, and far tastier way to join the celebration.

The activation brings PNC’s “Brilliantly Boring” brand platform to life in an unexpected way: as traffic cones began disappearing from Pittsburgh streets, longtime Pirates and PNC Park partner PNC -- and a known champion of avoiding unnecessary risks -- stepped in with a safer, smarter and far tastier way for fans to hoist the cone.

The collectible cone holders will be available inside PNC Park on August 16, September 6, and September 20, 2026, free with every waffle cone purchase, while supplies last.

Rennie has launched ‘Stop the Blame Game’, an integrated campaign from McCann London and Initiative Media promoting Rennie Wind Relief Pro, the brand’s first dedicated trapped wind product. Built around the humorous insight that dogs have been unfairly blamed for human flatulence for generations, the campaign uses Rennie’s trademark British humour to defend the country’s wrongly accused canines.

The campaign takes a documentary-style approach, featuring interviews, a staged protest and social content that tell the stories of dogs allegedly blamed for their owners’ digestive indiscretions. The work turns the familiar joke into a broader campaign idea, positioning Rennie Wind Relief Pro as the solution while giving dogs an opportunity to clear their names.

Launching in cinemas before expanding across TV, digital and social, the campaign features well-known voices including Pete Wicks, Susie Dent, Bill Bailey and Annette Badland. Each helps bring the stories of the wrongly accused dogs to life while reinforcing Rennie’s move into the wind relief category.

videos.description:
Every Little Helps speaks to the actions Tesco colleagues take every day to help customers and support their communities. These helps, big and small, make a real difference to people's lives.

Now Tesco is shining a light on how this works in practice through a new integrated campaign from BBH Dublin, 'That's Every Little Helps', which aims to pour new meaning into the brand's famous tagline.

The new brand direction brings 'Every Little Helps' to the forefront through a campaign that spans TV, OOH, radio, cinema, social, Clubcard, in store and online ads. The shift is designed to create a thoughtful people-focused connection with Tesco in a highly competitive retail landscape.

As customers expect more brands to prove their value, Tesco is shining a light on the meaningful everyday actions, or 'helps', that have always been delivered by Tesco colleagues all over the country for so many years.

The TVC, directed by Rich Hall at Riff Raff Films, focuses on a Tesco colleague as she moves through her busy day, all while revealing the many ways Tesco has helped to support local communities and customers across Ireland.

The nationwide OOH, that includes a Luas wrap and localised high impact 240$ OOH in Terenure, sees Tesco's iconic colleague badges reimagined to spotlight those unexpected 'helps'. These range from supporting more than 27,000 community projects with Tesco's Community Fund, to backing Irish suppliers like the McCanns Orchard in Louth, partnering with Children's Health Foundation and everyday helps like covering the cost of VAT on Tesco's own-brand suncream or donating repurposed end of life Tesco.ie delivery vans to local charities.

Collaborating with Irish illustrators for the OOH, including Tara O'Brien, Laura Callaghan, Stephen Heffernan and Darren Whittington, BBH Dublin created bespoke badge designs, built physical models and photographed them to create a distinctive visual style unique to the campaign.

On radio, Tesco colleagues become the voices of the campaign, sharing authentic stories of the ways their stores support customers and local communities. Broadcast nationally and locally, these stories will reinforce the campaign's central message through genuine, first hand experiences.

Marcos Gemal, Executive Creative Director at BBH Dublin, said: "It's a privilege to re-introduce a nation to such an iconic line. Our creative challenge was to showcase the breadth of Tesco's 'helps' with an entertaining and fun approach. So we chose to focus on a collection of unexpected 'helps', from big to small, that customers may not know about, bringing them to life in a warm and genuine Tesco way."

Katie Cunningham, Head of Brand Marketing at Tesco, said: "At Tesco, we've been helping Irish customers up and down the country for many years. This campaign puts an authentic spotlight on the community projects we support as never before, really showing how our many 'helps' make all the difference."

The campaign kicked off with OOH and radio, followed by TV, VOD, and online ads on 17 August. It features music by Irish artist Morgana from her new album 'The Whole Thing Was Very Very Emotional'.

videos.description:
Zales is redefining what a jewelry occasion looks like with “You Are the Occasion,” a new campaign centered on making quality fine jewelry accessible to everyone so women can express their personal style through pieces designed to be layered and lived in every day, no milestone required.

The campaign challenges the traditional perception of fine jewelry as something reserved for engagements, anniversaries, and gifting moments, positioning diamonds and jewelry as an integral part of daily self-expression and personal style. 

Developed in partnership with its creative agency of record, Anomaly, the work brings this cultural shift to life through a stylish, playful film where a simple fortune-cookie message “You Are the Occasion” moves from woman to woman, becoming a reminder to own confidence and individuality.

The campaign builds on Zales’ “Own It” brand platform, further establishing the brand as a destination for accessible diamond fashion and self-purchase. videos.description:
Hanes has launched ‘Get Comfortable’, a new campaign marking a significant shift in the brand’s messaging by showing how the comfort of its clothing gives people the confidence to handle awkward or embarrassing situations with ease. Created by Special U.S., the campaign introduces a bolder, more humorous tone as Hanes moves away from its traditional advertising approach. The launch is also accompanied by a refreshed logo that reflects the brand’s updated identity.

The campaign features four films depicting uncomfortable scenarios, including a man whose trousers are pulled down as a prank and a woman confidently shopping in her underwear. Rather than reacting with embarrassment, each character remains unfazed, reinforcing the idea that wearing Hanes provides an added sense of confidence. Another spot follows a trail of discarded clothing to reveal a couple in bed, with only their Hanes socks visible beneath the covers. The films were directed by Nick Ball and shot on film to give the work a distinctive visual style.

‘Get Comfortable’ is rolling out nationally across social, online video, retail, display and owned channels, supported by an out-of-home campaign in New York City. The creative extends the campaign’s playful tone with cheeky executions that reinforce the idea of confidence through comfort. The work represents Hanes’ first major campaign with agency partner Special U.S. and signals a new creative direction following HanesBrands’ acquisition by Gildan Activewear.

adidas has launched a campaign for its new Originals Sport womenswear collection, introducing a line designed to move effortlessly between sport and everyday life. Directed by Alana O'Herlihy and produced by Object & Animal, the campaign centres on the iconic Superstar tracksuit and stars singer Tate McRae, Argentine pop artist Emilia Mernes and US college volleyball player Harper Murray, each representing a different expression of performance and personal style.

By bringing together artists and an elite athlete, the campaign highlights the shared confidence and movement that connect their different worlds. Rather than treating each individual story separately, the films emphasise the common thread between them, positioning Originals Sport as a collection designed for women whose lives flow seamlessly between training, creativity and everyday life.

videos.description:
Launched ahead of England’s FIFA World Cup semi-final against Argentina, Nike’s latest campaign celebrates the unwavering optimism and enduring rituals of England fans, even after decades of tournament heartbreak. Created by Wieden+Kennedy London and directed by ILLIMITÉWORLD through Love Song, the film was conceived, shot and completed in under 48 hours following England’s quarter-final victory over Norway, allowing it to air before the semi-final.

The campaign reflects the belief that supporting England is about far more than results. Drawing on the country’s football history and the communal traditions that accompany every major tournament, the film captures the hope, superstition and shared conviction that football can always "come home", despite the setbacks that have defined England’s World Cup journey since its lone triumph in 1966.

Wayne Rooney leads the film, appearing in St George’s Cross face paint as he responds to a sceptic who suggests England fans are "out of their minds" for believing. Echoing Nike’s iconic 2006 ‘St Wayne’ campaign, Rooney replies, "We’re not mad. We’re English", reinforcing the campaign’s message that relentless belief is an essential part of England’s football identity. Rooney also fronts Nike’s collaborative England collection with streetwear brand Palace.

videos.description:
Grey London, as part of WPP’s team Vitale, has launched a new campaign for Parodontax built around the message ‘Spitting Blood Means Action.’ Directed by Finn Keenan through Riff Raff Films, the campaign uses the visual language and spectacle of martial arts cinema to challenge conventional healthcare advertising and raise awareness that bleeding gums can be a sign that action is needed.

The 90-second film begins with an ordinary tooth-brushing routine before quickly turning into an action sequence when the protagonist notices blood in the sink. She races to a pharmacy and becomes involved in a highly choreographed battle over the last tube of Parodontax, using toothbrushes as weapons and dental floss as a lasso. The concept plays on the familiar movie trope where characters shrug off blood and carry on, reframing that behaviour to show how people often dismiss bleeding gums in real life.

Launching across EMEA through 2026 and 2027, the campaign targets health-conscious adults who take an active approach to their wellbeing but may not recognise when specialist gum care is needed. With nearly half of adults expected to experience gum disease at some point, the work aims to make Parodontax the memorable choice for people experiencing gum problems by replacing the clinical tone of traditional dental advertising with humour, action and high-energy storytelling.

videos.description:
Liquid Death and goodwipes Join Forces to Launch Limited-Edition Flushable Wipes, Available Exclusively at Walmart

Liquid Death turned healthy beverages into a cultural movement. goodwipes has spent more than a decade modernizing the most overlooked room in the house with its mission of revolutionizing the restroom routine.

Now, the brands are joining forces to bring that same energy to the bathroom by launching one of the most unexpected brand collaborations of the summer: a limited-edition pack of flushable wipes, inspired by Liquid Death's sCREAM Soda.

Negotiated by partnership agency SonderCo, the collaboration goes beyond a licensing deal, with the brands reformulating goodwipes' signature product, infusing the flushable wipes with Liquid Death's Mountain Water and sCREAM Soda scent, along with goodwipes' gentle, skin-loving ingredients like aloe and vitamin E, to bring Liquid Death's signature edge to the beauty-and-booty-care world. 

Both brands have built loyal followings by bringing personality, innovation, and premium experiences to categories that traditionally lack all three. Rooted in a shared "Death to Dry" philosophy—whether that's dry mouths, dry wiping, or dry standards—the partnership extends Liquid Death and goodwipes' approach into personal care by creating a product fans can actually use.

The partnership comes to life through "The Buttler Sweepstakes," giving one lucky consumer the chance to win their own butt-wiping VIP service: a fully trained, live-in Buttler who will personally wipe their butt using Liquid Death x goodwipes sCREAM Soda wipes. 

The Sweepstakes launches alongside a brand film going live across Liquid Death and goodwipes' social channels on August 11. Featuring a tuxedo-clad “Buttler” who does nothing but wipe your butt, the comedic spot was co-ideated by both brands and produced in-house by Liquid Death, produced in the style of an SNL Happy Fun Ball parody, sending up the over-the-top infomercials of the category it's spoofing. The competition will run through August 31 (goodwipes.com/buttler). 

“We believe hydration shouldn't stop at your mouth. Combining goodwipes premium wipes with our 100% real Mountain Water and the scent of one of our most popular soda-flavor sparkling waters should make anyone feel #1 at #2, whether you have a live-in Buttler or not,” said Andy Pearson, Liquid Death VP of Creative. 

Meredith Diehn, SVP Marketing at goodwipes, added: “Consumers deserve better than dry, outdated experiences. From what you drink to how you wipe, the standard has always been too low, so we’ve joined forces with a brand who shares our ambition to disrupt the status quo, to help people truly upgrade their restroom routine. Made with real Liquid Death Mountain Water, aloe, and vitamin E, these wipes bring premium ingredients and a skincare-inspired approach to one of the most overlooked categories in personal care. This collab was always destined to happen—it just needed the right excuse, the right product, and one exceptionally classy 'Buttler.’” 

The limited-edition wipes launch exclusively in more than 4,000 Walmart stores nationwide on August 10 and will be available through January 2027.

videos.description:
Amazon India's campaign for the Great Freedom Sale 2026 directly highlights consumer shopping behaviours by focusing on relatable shopper personas. Created in collaboration with the agency- Schbang, produced by- Mothership Productions, and Directed by- Karan Shetty the campaign shifts away from just listing price cuts and instead focuses on how Indian consumers uniquely navigate major sales. 

The Core Campaign - Personas of Shoppers

The Shikari (hunter) Shopper: The ad film begins by using the iconic A-to-Z arrow from Amazon's logo to transition into the world of the Shikari (hunter) shopper, who is always on the look out for the best deals, like a hunter. 
The Tol-Mol (comparing) Shopper: Hyper-calculative buyers who refuses to hit checkout until they have stacked every possible coupon, bank discount, and cashback offer and have compared every possible deal. 
The Deal-Pe-Deal Shopper: The impulsive bargain hunters who continuously finds "one more great deal" to add to their cart. 
The FOMO Shopper: The shopper who continuously makes sure that he isn’t missing out. He is the Fear Of Missing Our (FOMO) shopper.  
The BOGO Shopper: The shopper who constantly tries to get a one plus one deal offer. They are the Buy One Get One (BOGO) Free shoppers.  

The campaign was narrated by a very honest voice over artist that spoke about these shoppers in a witty, charming style whilst being relatable making the montage moments in the campaign stand out.

videos.description:
When Ecuador faced Argentina in the South American Qualifiers, the biggest advantage wasn't on the pitch.

Naldo, an Argentine retailer, was the official sponsor of the Argentina National Team, with the rights to use the image of Lionel Messi, Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez, Lautaro Martínez and the rest of the world champions.

La Ganga had none of that.

So instead of competing with sponsorship money, it competed with creativity.

A few days before the match, La Ganga publicly challenged Naldo with a simple bet: if Ecuador won, Naldo would lend La Ganga the image rights of Argentina's players for one social media post. If Argentina won, La Ganga would publicly recognize Naldo as the winner.

The challenge quickly spread across social media, sports media and news outlets, turning a football match into a brand rivalry that fans wanted to follow.

Against all odds, Ecuador defeated Argentina.

Naldo honored the bet.

Within hours, La Ganga published a campaign featuring Messi, Lautaro Martínez, Emiliano Martínez and the reigning world champions—without paying a single dollar for their image rights.

What would normally require one of the most expensive sponsorship deals in football became the result of one bold creative idea.

The campaign generated nationwide conversation, earned extensive media coverage, sparked thousands of organic interactions and proved that, sometimes, the smartest way to compete against a sponsorship isn't buying one—it's making people talk about yours.

videos.description:
As investment in women's football continues to accelerate around the world, sports technology company Veo and Girls Academy (GA) have today launched a new hero film following the journey of 13 year old, Girls Academy player Emily Bernachea, dubbed as ‘women’s soccer’s next superstar’. It explores how the next generation of female footballers are being supported both on and off the pitch.

The two films are the latest chapter in the long-standing partnership between Veo and Girls Academy, one of the world's largest female youth football development platforms, which supports more than 36,000 players across 233 clubs in the United States.

More than just a personal story, Emily's journey reflects a much broader shift taking place across the women's game.

While attendances, investment and media attention continue to reach record highs, Veo and Girls Academy believe the next challenge is ensuring every talented young player has the opportunity to be seen, developed and recognised.

Today, every Girls Academy home fixture is captured using Veo, with matches uploaded to the Veo League Exchange, giving coaches, players and scouts access to video analysis and performance insights that were once reserved for elite professional environments.

The result is a development pathway where visibility becomes opportunity. Whether it's reviewing tactical performance, sharing highlights with college recruiters or helping players understand their own development, technology is becoming an essential part of modern player development.

The partnership extends beyond individual matches. At showcase events including the Girls Academy Champions Cup, Veo provides comprehensive video coverage across the tournament, ensuring every match is recorded and available for analysis. Across six days of competition featuring conference champions from across the country, every player has the opportunity to showcase their ability on one national platform.

Directed by Andreas Landgaard, the film follows Emily’s progression through Girls Academy, highlighting the commitment, resilience and support network behind every aspiring athlete. Despite her young age (13), the Florida United striker is already playing for the under 17s team and being touted as a top American youth prospect. It also reflects Girls Academy's wider philosophy that developing elite footballers means investing not only in technical ability, but in confident, resilient young women equipped to thrive throughout their lives. As women's football enters a new era of growth, Veo and Girls Academy believe investment must extend beyond the professional game and into the pathways that develop tomorrow's players. A second film titled ‘Mi querida nieta’ explores Emily’s relationship with her grandmother.

By combining elite coaching with AI-powered analysis and accessible performance technology, the partnership is helping create an environment where more young athletes can fulfil their potential.

videos.description:
For 31C's new Deep Packet Intelligence launch in Azerbaijan, we made something special.
31C's own logo is built from small data packet cubes. We took that concept further, pulling the cube out of the logo and making it the entire campaign theme. As a teaser, it appeared across dozens of LinkedIn profiles seven days before the event, creating that "Purple Feed" effect that led to hundreds of thousands of impressions and one question everywhere: "What is this?" Then we shared the news: a product launch.
On launch day, the cube seen in the video suddenly reached the real world — the CEO walked on stage holding the data packet itself to reveal the product: Odun One. One symbol, born in the brand, seen everywhere.
The event sold out and earned major exposure across all channels and media.

videos.description:
Commissioned by UN Women, Bystander is a tense, intimate short film exploring the split second where instinct, fear and responsibility collide.

Across a series of everyday settings - a bus stop late at night, a locker room after a match, an online gaming session, an open-plan office - we witness subtle but recognisable moments of harassment and boundary-crossing behaviour directed towards women. Nothing heightened. Nothing dramatised beyond reality. Just the familiar discomfort of something not quite right.

Each character faces the same internal question: intervene, or stay silent?
Told through restrained performances, tightening frames and immersive sound design, the film places the audience inside the pause before action, where rationalisation and conscience wrestle for control.

Rather than judging its characters, Bystander examines the psychology of inaction in the face of harassment and abuse towards women and the quiet realisation that silence, too, has consequences.

videos.description:
Universities have become remarkably sophisticated at standing still.

“Still Pending” is a cinematic brand film for MSM CampusOS that explores the hidden cost of waiting across higher education institutions.

MSM CampusOS is introduced not simply as another technology platform, but as an integrated operating model designed to help higher education institutions coordinate acquisition, admissions, marketing, engagement, operations and infrastructure.

The campaign uses dry humour, composed cinematography and restrained documentary-style storytelling to turn an operational challenge into an emotionally recognisable human experience.

The central message is simple:

Most delays are not caused by time.
They are caused by systems.
And systems can be redesigned.

MSM CampusOS
Run leaner. Focus deeper. Scale smarter.

videos.description:
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has unveiled the hero film for its new integrated ‘Feel Claim Confident’ campaign, created by M+C Saatchi Group UK. The push deliberately rejects the functional approach typically associated with financial services advertising in favour of cinematic, action movie-inspired creative.

The hero film launches today as the latest phase of a wider integrated campaign. Spanning BVOD, SVOD, online video, out-of-home, print, social and radio, the work encourages consumers to make their motor finance claim directly using the FCA's free tools while giving them the confidence to navigate the process themselves.

The campaign is designed to raise awareness among the holders of an estimated 12.1 million car finance agreements that took place before 2021, encouraging those who think they may be eligible to use the FCA's online tools to check whether they can make a claim. In a market crowded with competing claims services, it positions the FCA as the trusted source of clear, impartial guidance.

The launch comes as consumers continue to be targeted by hundreds of claims management companies and law firms promoting "No Win, No Fee" offers across multiple channels, creating confusion about where to turn, who to trust and whether they need someone else to act on their behalf.

Rather than focusing on the mechanics of making a claim, ‘Feel Claim Confident’ dramatises the confidence people feel once they've successfully completed it. The campaign replaces uncertainty with confidence, showing that making a claim yourself can be straightforward, empowering and rewarding.

At the heart of the campaign is a cinematic 30-second film, directed by David Wilson at Biscuit, that reimagines the iconic action movie bonnet slide through the lens of everyday British life. After completing their claim, ordinary people confidently slide across the bonnet of their own car, transforming a routine administrative task into a moment of achievement and empowerment.

Inspired by classic action films, the work combines bold movie-poster art direction with familiar settings including supermarket car parks, driveways and family cars, turning everyday people into unlikely action heroes. A deep, grindhouse-inspired voiceover and a rock ballad soundtrack complete the cinematic world, creating an epic tone that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

The bonnet slide becomes the campaign's distinctive visual signature, creating an ownable creative device that carries consistently across every touchpoint and gives the FCA a recognisable and emotionally engaging platform that stands apart from the category's typically functional communications.

videos.description:
Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com.

‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award.

Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools.

In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.”

‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...”

Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”.

The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. 

Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. 

Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand.

The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. 

The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide.

It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show.

videos.description:
To bring a global brand into South Korea, GUT Singapore didn't import a campaign, but built an entire brand world using a mark sitting inside NÜTRL's name all along.

The idea started with an untapped detail: the umlaut (Ü) in NÜTRL’s name. Reinterpreted as a smile, GUT Singapore transformed a simple typographic mark into NÜTRL’s defining visual signature, giving the global brand a warm, recognizable identity as it introduced itself to Korean consumers. 

That smile scaled into NÜTRL’s brand platform for Korea, Smile Üp. More than a campaign line, it expressed the brand’s mission in the market: to bring a little lightness and a little more reason to smile to Koreans. 

This came to life through an original music video featuring S.COUPS and MINGYU, where the artists don’t just endorse NÜTRL from the outside, but become part of the brand universe itself. By reimagining their hit single “For you” as “For Ü”, the music video introduces NÜTRL through music, entertainment and a vibrant visual universe inspired by the drink’s light and refreshing formulation and personality.

“For Ü” expands NÜTRL’s identity into a world filled with playful visual cues and recognizable Korean cultural references, giving the brand a distinctly Korean expression without losing the identity that travels with it globally. The result gives fans multiple ways to discover NÜTRL, combining functional product storytelling with entertainment people would choose to watch and share.

The music video sits at the heart of a social-first play, supported by out-of-home and on-ground activations, helping establish NÜTRL in one of Korea's fastest-growing and most competitive ready-to-drink categories.

Alongside the campaign, GUT Singapore led the redesign of NÜTRL's packaging for the Korean market, working with GUT Design to create a cohesive identity across every touchpoint.

“Korea is one of the most exciting and competitive ready-to-drink markets in the world, and we wanted to enter with impact. There was no better way to do that than collaborating with artists who genuinely shape the culture. Working with S.COUPS and MINGYU gave NÜTRL a level of cultural credibility and energy few launches ever get, positioning the brand right where music and culture meet.” said Alex Lambrecht, Marketing Vice President at Anheuser-Busch InBev.

"This launch was about much more than introducing a new drink," said Carlos Camacho, Chief Creative Officer at GUT Singapore. "The smile hidden in NÜTRL's own name gave us a way in, and music let us build a world people would choose to spend time in, rather than an ad they'd skip. Everything, down to turning “For you” into “For Ü”, came from that one idea."

The campaign marks another collaboration between GUT Singapore and leading Korean entertainment IPs and personalities, with past collaborations including Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars 2, Napoli Matfia, Moon Sang Hoon and more. Rather than announcing NÜTRL’s arrival with a conventional launch, the agency has applied its pop-culture-first instinct for a market entry, building a world fans across South Korea, Asia and beyond will choose to step into.

GUT Singapore x NÜTRL “Smile Up”

videos.description:
Dos Equis has launched a new campaign featuring Grammy and Latin Grammy-nominated band Fuerza Regida to coincide with the group's ‘This Is Our Dream’ stadium tour. Created as part of the brand’s ‘Stay Thirsty’ platform, the collaboration follows the return of ‘The Most Interesting Man in the World’ earlier this year and begins with a new TV spot, ‘The Most Interesting Origins’, before expanding into a series of fan activations throughout the summer.

The campaign cleverly blends fiction with real archival footage of Fuerza Regida, imagining an alternative history in which The Most Interesting Man was quietly present during the band's earliest days. By weaving the iconic character into genuine moments from the group's beginnings, the film celebrates the band's rise while reinforcing themes of curiosity, ambition and taking risks. The collaboration also builds on Dos Equis' successful partnership with Fuerza Regida from the previous year.

Timed to the band's stadium tour, the campaign positions the collaboration as a meeting of two cultural icons, using storytelling to connect the legacy of The Most Interesting Man with one of today's most influential music acts. Through exclusive fan experiences and content, Dos Equis continues to evolve its long-running brand platform while celebrating bold choices and the pursuit of living interestingly.

videos.description:
From Cinnamon Toast Crunch loyalists to Lucky Charms obsessives, General Mills cereals have inspired devoted fans for generations. And now, those fans have something BIG to rally around. General Mills is passing the ball to sports legend and cereal superfan Shaquille O'Neal, to bring his big personality and love of competition to the first ever Biggest Fan Contest — inviting fans to prove their cereal devotion for the opportunity to win epic prizes, exclusive merch and unforgettable experiences inspired by General Mills Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Lucky Charms, Reese's Puffs and Honey Nut Cheerios cereals.

"I have been eating cereal my whole life, and I'm still just as excited about it now as I was when I was young," said Shaquille O'Neal. "Lucky Charms has always been a favorite — those marshmallows never get old to me. This contest is a chance to celebrate that same excitement in fans everywhere who love cereal as much as I do."

From cereal-themed tattoos to cereal bars at weddings, fans have found bold ways to show off their cereal love for years. With the Biggest Fan Contest, General Mills is giving their superfans the opportunity to prove their passion by uploading a photo or video and sharing why they deserve the title of Biggest Fan.

The competition will feature one massive grand prize plus four cereal-inspired fan experiences and a year's supply of their favorite cereal:

• Grand Prize: A BIG trip to Shaq's Fun House, including two VIP tickets and $1,000 spending cash, plus a BIG cash prize of $20K and a meet and greet with Shaq.
• Lucky Charms Pot of Gold: A cauldron complete with two 1 oz gold bars along with VIP tickets and a trip for two to Shaq's Fun House.
• Cinnamon Toast Crunch Cinnafan Cave: A fully decked-out, Cinnadusted fan cave for the ultimate game day setup and tickets to Shaq's Fun House.
• Reese's Puffs VIP Pass: A "Very Important Puff" experience to Shaq's Fun House plus $1,500 spending cash and a ride in style to one of the most talked-about parties of football's biggest game, along with a custom Reese's Puffs turntable and sound system.
• Honey Nut Cheerios "Bowl" Hot Tub: A BIG Honey Nut Cheerios bowl-inspired hot tub paired with Cheerios-themed lawn chairs, plus tickets to Shaq's Fun House.

Fans who act fast can score even more — early entrants will unlock access to limited-edition brand-inspired merch, available while supplies last.

Hitting shelves this August, shoppers can also find a lineup of Fandemonium Faves including limited-edition boxes of Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Lucky Charms, Reese's Puffs and Honey Nut Cheerios featuring custom tattoos inspired by each cereal so fans can show off their spirit. Plus, when shoppers spend $25 on select General Mills products, they can receive $10 back* by uploading their receipt at ScoreWithGeneralMills.com.

"Our cereal fans bring incredible passion and personality to the brands they love, and we believe we have some of the best fans out there," said Megan Brooks, Business Unit Director for Family Favorite Cereals at General Mills. "With Shaq bringing his larger-than-life energy to the Biggest Fan Contest, we wanted to create a fun way for people to join in, show their love for their favorite cereals and compete for some seriously unforgettable prizes."

Through December 31, 2026, fans can visit BiggestFanContest.com to enter for a chance to win. The top 100 highest-scoring entries will be evaluated by cereal content creator Ami Moyal, known online as @cereallife and recognized for his love of cereal culture and fandom. From there, Shaq will select the grand prize winner, who will be announced on National Cereal Day, March 7, 2027.

Beginning Monday, September 1, 2026, fans can see Shaq alongside a surprise lineup of cereal superfans in a new ad spot rolling out across TV, streaming and social platforms nationwide.

videos.description:
AI is making more of our everyday decisions and when people rely on it without thinking twice, the results can be hilariously human. From a politician accidentally reading AI-generated prompts aloud during a legislative speech to professionals sending emails with chatbot instructions still intact, AI mishaps are quickly becoming a familiar part of modern life.

The timing couldn't be more interesting for Snickers, whose Eulogy spot explores a similar cultural truth: as AI becomes part of everyday life, the line between human and machine is getting blurrier, and sometimes hilariously so.

In the film, a eulogist reads AI prompts verbatim during a heartfelt speech, turning a familiar AI mishap into a classic You're Not You When You're Hungry moment.

videos.description:
Rice Krispies Treats expands its “Treat Your Inner Child” campaign with a new pair of spots directed by Voyager’s Grayson Whitehurst, leaning further into a playful, escapist world that blurs the line between everyday routine and imagination.    

Created as a second installment of the campaign introduced in 2025, the new work builds on the idea that a Rice Krispies Treats bar can spark a small break from routine, unlocking a more spontaneous, carefree state of mind. The product serves as the entry point into each surreal world, inspiring environments built from its ingredients, textures and playful spirit.  

Each spot begins in a familiar, more serious setting before quickly shifting into a surreal fantasy. In one, a man stuck on hold at his desk takes a bite of a Rice Krispies Treats bar and is transported into a world made entirely of its ingredients, ziplining through towering crispy rice and marshmallow mountains alongside animated goats that spring to life mid-yodel. In another, a routine elevator ride transforms into a marshmallow-filled world, where a woman floats and bounces through massive, cloud-like forms after tasting a Rice Krispies Treats Homestyle bar, subtly highlighting the product’s larger size in comparison to the brand's core offering.  

The spots move quickly from ordinary routines into surreal fantasy environments, balancing large-scale visual worlds with grounded performances and tactile production design. Shot in Romania alongside BBDO and local production partners, the campaign was built to deliver cinematic transitions within condensed 15- and 6-second formats.

“We wanted each spot to capture that private moment when routine breaks and joy feels easy again,” shares Grayson. “The fantasy was a physical expression of that feeling. So, we approached everything as tangible and real: practical builds, sculpted textures, grounded performances, with VFX used to expand the world rather than replace it. Because the spots had to work in 15s and 6s, every choice was about entering imagination quickly while still letting the release breathe and giving the humor of each moment room to land.”

Each spot closes with the tagline, “Treat Your Inner Child.”

“Enjoyment Until the Last Bell” is an integrated Back-to-School content campaign created and produced by Feediper for Pemina. The idea was built around two sides of a lunchbox: the care and effort a mother puts into preparing a school snack, and the enjoyment a child feels when opening it at school.

Pemina appears as a practical solution for preparing an appealing school snack in limited time.

The hero film moves to the classroom. When the bell rings, every student rushes out except one boy, who stays behind to enjoy his Pemina lunchbox in secret. His friends soon return and catch him keeping all the good food to himself, turning the familiar joke of eating without sharing into a playful and memorable product moment.

Three carousel sets extend the idea through colorful, top-down lunchbox combinations featuring a range of Pemina products alongside fruit, vegetables, and familiar school-day sides.

Together, the campaign connects the care behind every lunchbox with the joy of eating it, positioning Pemina as an easy, appealing, and enjoyable part of the school routine—delivering “Enjoyment Until the Last Bell.”

Created and produced by Feediper for Pemina.

videos.description:
Today’s women are moving through life with ambition, instinct, humor, and momentum. They show up differently in every moment, moving fluidly between responsibility, adventure, and spontaneity without being defined by any one role. There are many sides of her nature.

That unstoppable nature is the insight and inspiration behind Chomps' new national campaign, ‘For All Sides of Her Nature,’ from creative agency nice&frank, debuting today Friday, July 31. 

The campaign celebrates the women helping shape modern protein culture, not by optimizing for one narrow version of wellness, but by using protein to fuel fuller, more dynamic lives. Through three films inspired by the visual language of nature documentaries, For All Sides of Her Nature observes women navigating everyday moments with instinct, resourcefulness, determination, and humor. 

The work builds on Chomps’ ‘Take Bigger Bites’ platform, celebrating what Chomps helps make possible: more confidence, momentum and freedom to embrace every side of life.

The media buy will feature high-impact placements around marquee cultural and sports moments; including NFL games, the NBA Black Friday game, Dancing with the Stars, and Amazon's Black Friday event, while reaching audiences across leading streaming and linear networks like Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, Peacock, Disney+, ESPN, CBS, Bravo, TNT, and more.

As protein continues to dominate grocery, wellness, and cultural conversations with the top 3 fastest growing brands being protein-based*, women are increasingly driving demand, seeking convenient, high-quality protein that supports active, multidimensional lifestyles. 

Stacey Hartnett, SVP of Marketing, Chomps:
“Women are helping drive the growth of protein because it supports the way they are already living full, active lives that move constantly between ambition, adventure, responsibility, and spontaneity. Protein has become an essential part of how they fuel themselves and those around them, and we saw an opportunity to celebrate the full range of who they already are and the many ways strength shows up in their lives. ‘For All Sides of Her Nature’ reflects the instinct, confidence, and momentum we see in the women driving our brand forward and the role Chomps can play in making one choice in a full day feel a little easier. It is the next expression of ‘Take Bigger Bites:’ an invitation to embrace every side of yourself and keep moving toward what’s next.”

Chelsea Lee, Senior Art Director, nice&frank:
“We were inspired by the instinctive, powerful, and often surprising ways women move through the world. The nature documentary format gave us a playful way to observe those moments with curiosity and admiration, elevating everyday behaviors into something bold, cinematic, and worth celebrating. Rather than define each woman by a single role, we wanted to show characters who feel layered, capable and unpredictable, because that is what makes them so compelling.”

Reilly Schlitt, Associate Creative Director, nice&frank:
“The documentary-style narration made our stories feel more real. Documentaries don’t force a narrative: they observe what’s already there. So, the creative goal became representing daily moments with the same reverence you’d see in your favorite documentary. Plus, leaning into the genre allowed us to have a sense of humor, while still celebrating all the different roles women naturally take on.”

videos.description:
Motion Sickness and Sealord have launched ‘We Love Fish’, a new brand platform designed to encourage New Zealanders to embrace their love of fish without embarrassment. Built around the idea of “fishame” — the guilt or discomfort people may feel about eating fish because of its smell, mess or frozen format — the campaign uses humour to challenge the social and practical barriers that can stop people from eating more seafood.

Directed by Damien Shatford through The Sweetshop, the launch film, ‘The Manifishto’, follows a weathered skipper determined to cure the nation of fishame. He encounters people hiding their fish habits in public, including a man concealing an open tin of tuna on a bus, a woman hiding after reheating fish in an office microwave and a child questioning a hoki fillet at the dinner table. His solution is simple: stop hiding and hold that fish high with pride.

Sealord says the platform aims to make eating fish feel easier, more confident and more socially acceptable while reinforcing its role as a brand that helps New Zealanders enjoy more seafood. The hero film is supported by a wider campaign across TV, digital, social and out-of-home, with media handled by PHD Aotearoa.

Minute Maid has extended its long-running ‘Bring the Juice’ platform to its Zero Sugar range for the first time with a new campaign celebrating the small victories of everyday adult life. Created by WPP Open X, led by Studio X and RSA Films, the work highlights how a little positivity, confidence and a glass of Minute Maid Zero Sugar can transform life’s everyday compromises into moments worth celebrating.

videos.description:
Feediper created and produced this 30-second cinema campaign for FirePower to build brand awareness and position the energy drink as a natural part of the high-energy moments Gen Z share.

The film opens from inside an ice-filled cooler, placing the product at the center of the story from the very first frame. From there, a FirePower can moves through a connected series of consumption occasions: a camping trip, a football watch party at home, a lip-sync moment, a poolside gathering, an outdoor party with a DJ, and finally a cinema screening. A stylized CGI passage through ice and the inner world of the product connects the live-action environments.

Music was conceived as a narrative device rather than simply added in post-production. Feediper wrote and produced an original Persian-language track in a distinctly Gen Z voice, then built the film’s scenes around its lyrics. Product-led match cuts synchronize every throw, spin, placement, and sip with the beat, transforming separate locations into one continuous, high-energy journey while keeping the FirePower can as the visual anchor throughout.

Built around the message “Every moment gets better with FirePower,” the campaign was released in Iran on July 15, 2026. The film ran as a cinema pre-roll before screenings of Estakhr, a major Iranian theatrical release directed by acclaimed filmmaker Soroush Sehat.

The campaign formed part of FirePower’s broader partnership with Estakhr. FirePower served as an official sponsor of the feature, with the product integrated into selected scenes. Running Feediper’s film immediately before the feature extended the brand’s presence from in-film product placement to a dedicated pre-show cinema experience.

videos.description:
Café Bustelo, the iconic coffee brand known for its bold and rich Latin flavor, is introducing Game Face, a limited-time campaign and program that invites fans to show up for what they love through coffee, country pride and bold self-expression.

Game Face brings fandom to life with over one million limited-edition collectible coffee cans celebrating countries tied to the heritage of Café Bustelo – Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico; each paired with temporary face-tattoo kits featuring artwork created by local artists that reflects the countries' unique culture. Every Game Face tattoo features intricate creative elements that celebrate and honor the culture, heritage and symbolism of each country.

The countries reflected in Game Face are each based on the heritage of Café Bustelo and how the brand continues to deliver coffee that fans know and love today. In Latin culture, passion shows up loudest through sports. With Game Face, Café Bustelo is giving fans a new way to wear their pride on their face on game day, pairing country-inspired designs with the brand's signature bold Latin flavor.

"Café Bustelo is all about celebrating Latin culture and the passions that make it so vibrant and exciting," said Emily Lucci, Brand Marketing Coffee Vice President. "In this spirit, the Game Face campaign honors countries that are synonymous with our brand through the inspiration of art and sports. We're proud to launch this Game Face campaign and give fans new ways to express their pride this summer."

Café Bustelo is inviting fans everywhere to get their Game Face on this June and July and proudly show their support.

What is the Café Bustelo Game Face campaign?
Café Bustelo Game Face is a limited-edition campaign celebrating Latin passion, sports and self-expression. It features collectible coffee cans inspired by four countries close to the Café Bustelo heritage, each including a Game Face tattoo kit that invites fans to wear their pride on their face on game day.

What limited-edition items are included in the Game Face launch?
The launch includes limited-edition Café Bustelo coffee cans inspired by Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico, all countries tied to the heritage of Café Bustelo and how the brand delivers coffee that fans know and love today. Every can includes a vibrant, collectible design and one Game Face tattoo kit inside the lid. Artists from Argentina, Brasil, Colombia and Mexico created designs inspired by each country's unique visual language, incorporating elements from local flora and fauna, national iconography and culturally significant patterns, symbols and colors.

When and where are Game Face coffee cans available?
Café Bustelo Game Face coffee cans are available at retailers nationwide beginning June 1, 2026, encouraging fans to visit stores to discover the limited-edition designs. Availability may vary by retailer, and the cans are offered for a limited time while supplies last.

What is included in the Game Face tattoo kit?
Each collectible coffee can contains a country-inspired Game Face tattoo kit with temporary face tattoos designed to help fans show their passion and pride on game day. Each design draws inspiration from the vibrant face paint worn by the most passionate Latin American sports fans. The limited-edition Café Bustelo cans feature custom-engineered packaging that integrates the tattoo kit directly onto the product lid, turning a traditional coffee can into an interactive fan experience.

videos.description:
Ciao Energy — When France’s Biggest Creators Become Co-Founders

In May 2026, three of France’s most influential content creators — Squeezie, Inoxtag and Léna Situations — unveiled an unexpected collaboration: not a content project or a one-off partnership, but a new energy drink brand, Ciao Energy. The launch brought together three complementary personalities and their combined communities of several tens of millions of followers, turning creator influence into a fully-fledged consumer brand.

Ciao Energy is positioned as a less sugary and more transparent alternative to traditional energy drinks, with six original flavors including White Peach, Apricot Raspberry, Kiwi Cucumber and Double Lychee. The brand builds on Squeezie’s existing Ciao universe, launched with Ciao Kombucha in 2025, while giving Inoxtag and Léna Situations an equal role as co-founders rather than simply endorsing the product.

The collaboration also carries a strong personal dimension. Inoxtag had been working for several years on his own energy drink project, Gang Potion, but struggled to bring it to market. With the support and expertise of Squeezie and Léna Situations, the idea was finally transformed into Ciao Energy — with Double Lychee becoming the flavor associated with Inoxtag.

Beyond the product itself, Ciao Energy illustrates a broader shift in the creator economy: creators are no longer simply media channels for brands. They are increasingly becoming entrepreneurs, co-founders and brand builders, bringing together audience, cultural relevance and product development. Ciao Energy is a particularly strong example of this evolution, combining three major creator profiles around a shared brand vision rather than a traditional influencer partnership.

videos.description:
Vimto is returning to screens this summer with a campaign that's bold, fruity and every bit as irresistible as the drink itself.
The campaign is designed to drive penetration by targeting those who haven't yet tried Vimto - and tempting them in with the brand's trademark quirky charm and some flirty banter.
Quiet Storm brought the campaign to life through a series of online executions that playfully parody classic seduction tropes with a wink. Taking centre stage, the Vimto drink appears as an irresistibly charming suitor, speaking directly to viewers: "Can I be your big juicy crush? Your usual drink doesn’t need to know.”…"
It's provocative enough to capture attention, playful enough to raise a smile, and distinctly, unapologetically Vimto.
Building on the brand's previous "Love the Taste", "Love at First Taste" continues to position Vimto as one of Britain's most distinctive and tempting soft drinks - a cheeky challenge to the nation to give it a try.
The campaign runs across an integrated mix of channels, including out-of-home, bus wraps, digital, social media and online video, with executions on YouTube and Bliss digital advertising. Adding an unmissable in-store dimension, the campaign will feature across 28 million packs with limited edition packaging carrying cheeky chat-up lines.  It launches 20 July 2026 and continues through to the end of August. 
Peter Robinson, Senior Brand Manager, Vimto, said, “Millions of drinkers already know and love the unmistakable taste of Vimto, but believe it or not, there are still people out there who haven’t tried it yet.
This summer, we’ll be tempting new drinkers to give in to the irresistible taste of Vimto and give it a try knowing that once they’ve tasted it, it will be love at first taste. We’ll be doing this with a brand new set of ads and limited edition packaging which really leverage the cheeky sense of humour Vimto is known and loved for."
Massimo Fiori, Client Development Director at Quiet Storm, said: "Vimto is a brand overflowing with charm and personality.‘Love at First Taste’ gave us a brilliant opportunity to lean into something flirtatious, tempting and unmistakably Vimto."
‘Love at First Taste’ marks the conclusion of Quiet Storm's creative partnership with Vimto, following 8 years of collaboration.

videos.description:
PepsiCo® continues to expand its snack portfolio in Mexico with the launch of PopCorners®, a product designed to redefine one of the category's most familiar formats. Featuring a distinctive triangular shape, a unique texture and a bold personality, PopCorners® invites consumers to experience popcorn in an entirely new way.
For decades, popcorn seemed to have reached its final form. PopCorners® challenges that assumption by proving that even the most established products can evolve. Its signature triangular shape breaks category conventions while becoming the symbol of a new snacking experience created for consumers looking for products that deliver both enjoyment and fun.
The launch is driven not only by product innovation but also by changing consumer expectations. PopCorners® was created for people who enjoy discovering brands with personality, originality and a fresh perspective. The idea is simple: changing the shape can also change the experience, transforming an everyday snack into something completely unexpected.
That insight became the foundation of the brand's launch campaign, developed together with independent creative agency Zurda México. The campaign turns the product's unconventional shape into the center of the conversation, introducing PopCorners® as a playful, irreverent and approachable brand.
Creatively, the campaign uses the triangular shape as its strongest brand asset, placing it across different worlds and characters to reinforce one simple idea: when a category evolves, the way we talk about it should evolve too.
"You can't launch a triangular product with a square campaign. That's why we brought in cavemen, Egyptians, superheroes and even an astronaut," said Jorge Cordero and Rubén Cabezas, Creative Directors at Zurda México.
As part of the project, Zurda México developed the brand strategy, positioning, creative platform, visual identity and a comprehensive content ecosystem to support PopCorners®' launch in the Mexican market.
"At PopCorners, we believe that even the most familiar products can be reinvented. We're arriving in Mexico to challenge the idea that popcorn always has to be round and to show that a different shape can also deliver a completely new texture and flavor experience. This launch reflects PepsiCo's ongoing commitment to innovation and to expanding its portfolio with products that respond to evolving consumer preferences. With PopCorners, we want to connect with people looking for something different, surprising and full of personality, because innovation also means challenging what we've always taken for granted," said Juan Cuevas, Marketing Director for PopCorners Mexico.
With the arrival of PopCorners®, PepsiCo® continues to strengthen its snack portfolio with products designed to meet evolving consumer preferences while reinforcing its commitment to innovation across the category. PopCorners® enters the Mexican market with a proposition that combines a distinctive identity, a different snacking experience and a campaign that invites consumers to rethink everything they thought they knew about popcorn.

videos.description:
Weight Watchers has launched ‘Here At Every Point’, a 60-second film directed by Martina Magorin of Golden LA that takes a more personal approach to the weight loss category. Created with Anomaly, the film follows a woman who, between work and motherhood, has gradually lost touch with an earlier version of herself. When she discovers a favourite pair of jeans and an old Polaroid, she begins reflecting on her journey through false starts, small victories and early-morning weigh-ins.

The campaign is designed to speak to the growing GLP-1 landscape while positioning Weight Watchers as a broader support system that combines nutrition, coaching, medication and community. Rather than focusing solely on physical transformation, the film centres on accountability, connection and helping people rediscover confidence in their everyday lives. Magorin describes it as a story about finding your way back to the version of yourself that feels comfortable enough to say yes and fully enjoy life.

Magorin and director of photography Sean Conaty used an intimate visual approach, relying on eye-level framing, simple locked-off shots and gentle handheld camera work to keep the focus on the character and performance. The wardrobe also evolves throughout the story, moving from layers and softer shapes that help the character hide towards more colourful and intentional clothing that reflects her growing confidence. ‘Here At Every Point’ is rolling out nationally across broadcast, digital and social platforms.

videos.description:
Prioritizing your health shouldn’t wait for tomorrow — your future self isn’t just an abstract concept, but the person you could start becoming today. 

That’s the idea behind the new Jarrow Formulas campaign, created in partnership with Betty, a Quad agency. Instead of focusing on external motivations for wellness or on product ingredients alone, the spots dramatize the connection between today’s decisions and your future health span by showing a man competing with his future self. 

The campaign, titled “Put more in today. Get more out tomorrow,” launched July 15 and marks the first creative expression of Jarrow’s comprehensive brand transformation. 

Designed to bring the new Jarrow brand world to life, the campaign translates the brand’s scientific credibility into a motivational message about living better, longer by taking Jarrow as part of taking care of yourself. It also establishes a long-term creative platform that can extend across paid media, social, Amazon, DTC, PR, influencer partnerships, retailer materials, and future product launches.

Informed by a year of consumer research, Jarrow and Betty realized a key cultural truth: optimizing health is no longer a niche behavior. It’s the new normal. The creative strategy focused on helping people proactively improve their lifestyles for the long-term rather than simply avoiding health problems, and the execution shows the payoff when you start chasing down your healthier future self today.

videos.description:
The Austrian Bike Bell – Austria develops the world’s friendliest bike bell.
As the world's friendliest holiday destination, Austria is launching a specially developed multi-tone bike bell designed to make streets around the world just a little friendlier. Created by Austria Tourism in collaboration with Wien Nord Serviceplan and renowned austrian music experts, the Austrian Bike Bell serves as a symbol of the diverse cycling experiences Austria has to offer.
The fact that the sound of a traditional bike bell often creates stress on the streets has become an increasingly relevant topic. As Europe's friendliest travel destination (according to Condé Nast Traveller) and a country with a rich musical heritage, Austria is uniquely positioned to make a statement. The goal was to create a new sound inspired by the moments people experience while cycling through Austria – joyful laughter, clinking glasses, warm greetings – and transform them into a tone with a distinctly positive and friendly character.
Together with internationally renowned composer and music expert Walter Werzowa, Austria Tourism developed a fully mechanical bell system. Four differently tuned bells ring simultaneously, producing a rich multi-tone sound that feels more like a small musical gesture than a conventional bike bell. The composition is based on authentic sounds from Austria, translating the country's hospitality into a distinctive new acoustic identity.
The Austrian Bike Bell is intentionally presented as a gift to the world. To make the idea as accessible as possible, Austria Tourism has made all construction files available free of charge as open source. The 3D-print blueprints can be downloaded at austrianbikebell.com, allowing anyone to build, adapt, and locally manufacture the bell anywhere in the world. The website also offers insights into the creative process and the story behind the project.
The Austrian Bike Bell launched simultaneously in Germany, the Netherlands, and the Czech Republic. The international rollout was supported by local activations, test rides, and collaborations with influencers who introduced the bell in real-life cycling situations. The campaign is accompanied by a launch film, produced together with ForaUltra, which tells the story of the Austrian Bike Bell as an artistic journey through Austria's soundscape, bringing together music, hospitality, and the cycling experience in an emotional way.

videos.description:
The Heat Can't Beat Us 

How Midea Found a Different Way to Tell an Iraqi Story 

When people think about advertising air conditioners, the formula is almost written for you. 

Show the heat. 

Show people struggling. 

Introduce the product. 

Everyone feels better. 

It's a formula we've all seen before, and honestly, we could have followed it too. But as we started talking about Midea's summer campaign, something didn't sit right with us. 

Yes, Iraq is incredibly hot. During the summer, temperatures climb well above 50°C, and air conditioning isn't a luxury, it's something people genuinely rely on every day. But when we thought about our own experiences of summer, and the people around us, we realized the heat wasn't the whole story. 

Life doesn't pause because it's hot. 

People still go to work. Markets are still crowded. Street vendors still prepare drinks for long lines of customers. Families still go shopping together. Friends still meet by the river. Kids still find ways to cool off. 

Summer wasn't something Iraqis were trying to escape. 

It was something they had learned to live with. 

That realization became the starting point for everything that followed. 

Instead of asking ourselves how we could make another air conditioner commercial, we started asking a different question. 

What does summer actually feel like when you live in Iraq? 

For a while, we stopped thinking about the product altogether. Instead, we started paying attention. 

The more we looked around, the more we noticed the little moments we normally take for granted. 

The sound of ice being crushed into a glass of shanina. 

A juice vendor pouring another drink before the previous customer had even walked away. 

A watermelon being sliced open at a market. 

The mist of water spraying over people trying to cool down. 

The familiar buzz of traffic on a hot afternoon. 

A scooter carrying giant blocks of ice through the city. 

An old man sitting outside with a cup of hot tea, completely comfortable despite the temperature. 

A family walking through the front door after grocery shopping, immediately relaxing the moment the cool air reaches them. 

Individually, these moments don't seem particularly remarkable. Together, they tell you exactly where you are. They're the little details every Iraqi knows without ever really thinking about them. 

At some point during those conversations, someone said something that changed the whole direction of the campaign. 

“What if summer isn't just something you see?” 

Summer has its own soundtrack. You hear it before you even notice it. 

That single idea became the film. The crack of ice. The splash of water. The rustle of clothes catching cool air. The hum of an air conditioner quietly filling a room. Every location had its own note, and together they became one continuous piece of music—which is how Symphony of Summer found its name. 

One of my favorite parts of this project wasn't even in the final edit. It was being out in Baghdad while we were filming. 

Because we weren't shooting on closed sets or isolated locations, people naturally became curious. They stopped to watch. 

A lot of them wanted to know why we were paying so much attention to details most people walk past without a second glance, why a crew would spend that long filming ice being crushed into a glass, or a vendor pouring juice. The scale of it made people assume this had to be something bigger than a single campaign. More than a few were convinced we were shooting an entire series. 

Others simply smiled and stayed for a few minutes before continuing with their day. 

There was something special about that. We weren't creating an artificial version of Iraqi summer. We were standing right in the middle of it. 

Looking back, those interactions reminded us why authenticity mattered so much for this campaign. If the people living these moments recognized themselves in what we were filming, we knew we were heading in the right direction. 

When the film was finally finished, we realized it wasn't really about air conditioning. 

It was about recognition. 

It was about seeing familiar moments on screen and thinking, “That's us.” 

The product still had an important role to play, but it didn't need to dominate every frame. It simply became part of a story that already existed. 

I think that's what made Symphony of Summer different. 

We didn't begin with a script. 

We didn't begin with the product. 

We began by observing. By listening. 

By paying attention to the sounds, routines, and little rituals that make an Iraqi summer feel uniquely Iraqi. 

Because in the end, no product wins a real place in someone's home. It has to earn a place in their story first and this summer, ours got to sound like Iraq.
